national.name: Bank code, branch code and account number

note: HSBC, the largest bank in Hong Kong (read 2026-10-30): a payer chooses the bank by its three-digit code (HSBC's is 004) and enters the 10- or 12-digit HSBC account number, whose first 3 digits are the branch code, followed by a 7- or 9-digit account number. Other banks' lengths vary and no Hong Kong Interbank Clearing or HKMA rule fixing them was read (HKICL's site answered with an empty page), so HSBC's twelve-digit form (branch 3, account 9) is written. No check digit is stated.

sources.title: HSBC Hong Kong, Help: transfers and payments FAQ
sources.said: Please advise your payer to choose HSBC (bank code 004) as the payee’s bank or receiving bank, then enter your 10- or 12-digit HSBC account number in the payee account number field. The first 3 digits of your HSBC account number is the branch code, followed by a 7- or 9-digit account number.

sources.title: HSBC Hong Kong, Customer information sheet for inward payments to Hong Kong
sources.said: Account number of HSBC HK must be 10 or 12 digits. Branch code is the first 3 digits and the following 7-9 digits
